results.text:
## Utility package

[`ResourceLoader`](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/util/ResourceLoader.java#L31) loads `ResourceBundle`s for the default or explicit locale/class loader. On `MissingResourceException` it prints a stack trace, reports to stderr, calls `System.exit(1)`, then nominally returns null. Callers such as `CommonResources` initialize bundles statically, so missing bundles can terminate application startup. Resource selection and fatal-failure behavior are part of the startup contract.

[`Encoder.hexEncode`](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/util/Encoder.java#L24) produces two uppercase hexadecimal characters per byte. [`RandomKeyGenerator.generate`](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/util/RandomKeyGenerator.java#L38) uses `SecureRandom`, rejects lengths below one, and actually generates only uppercase A–Z (despite its comment claiming digits too). `formatKey` inserts hyphens before each character whose zero-based index is divisible by four; it does not validate key shape. [`StringUtilities.getFormattedMessage`](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/util/StringUtilities.java#L27) defaults to 120 characters, uses space-delimited tokens for long lines, and can normalize/collapse whitespace on those lines; short lines are appended unchanged. Do not treat this as a lossless text formatter.

question.question: Where are saved user preferences serialized to disk and loaded on startup?
question.notes: savePreferences and loadPreferences use preferences.ser and Java object streams.

results.text:
## Minimal-startup boundary and phase order

For the first modernization checkpoint, preserve the existing data directory, serialized preferences/favorites, raw configured JKS paths, certificate aliases, server-certificate trust UI, and FTPS session modes. Use a fresh temporary user home, not the developer's profile, and first characterize startup and ordinary FTP without exposing real credentials. Validate serialized preferences and favorites before touching TLS, then validate existing JKS load/save against copied synthetic stores, then run controlled local FTPS cases. Only after that baseline should implementation work change provider selection, trust validation, password protection, storage format, or client identity handling. Each of those changes has separate migration and user-visible behavior implications.

The repository-level modernization plan should keep storage migration, TLS policy, archive security, and Swing worker replacement in ordered, independently reviewable phases. Do not combine these changes under a general cleanup step.

### 1. Startup, session selection, preferences and favorites

Launch the desktop application with an isolated temporary `user.home`. Verify that first startup creates usable default preferences; a session begins disconnected, can open multiple tabs, and toolbar/menu commands apply to the selected tab. Save and reload representative locale/theme, local directory, passive mode, extension transfer mapping, proxy disabled, certificate-store path, and update-check setting. Add, edit, sort, reject duplicate, connect from, and delete favorites; verify fields such as label, host, port, user, account, client/parser choice, initial directories, commands and SSL mode survive the favorites round trip. Exercise connection validation at port endpoints 0 and 65535, required fields containing only whitespace, and implicit SSL port validation only when that mode is selected. Confirm whitespace is used for validation but approved host/user/password/path/command strings retain their entered value. Never assert real credentials or use an actual proxy/server.

The current persistence formats are Java serialization for `preferences.ser` and a `SealedObject` wrapper for `favorites.ser`; tests should use synthetic values and a fresh temporary home. Include compatibility fixtures only if a safe synthetic legacy plaintext favorite list can be generated. Treat the fixed-key wrapper, object deserialization, and plaintext preference password fields as current storage facts, not a desired security contract. The suite should verify the migration policy selected for implementation rather than freeze unsafe storage indefinitely.

Favorites hold host label/address/port, user/password/account, FTP client and listing parser classes, initial local/remote directories, passive mode, login-time commands and SSL/data-channel choices. The manager sorts favorites, rejects duplicate names, supports add/edit/delete and connects the selected host in the active session (creating a session if none exists). `JFTP.DATA_HOME` is `${user.home}/.jftp/data`; global preferences and favorites are Java serialized files there. `JFTPPreferences` declares `serialVersionUID = 4316033315068041786L`, `RemoteHost` declares `-3213664402994404410L`, and `Favorite` declares `-8742993458243896488L`. The top-level saved containers are `JFTPPreferences` and the favorites list; `JFTP`/`FavoritesManager` define no additional explicit serialized-container version identifier. `RemoteHost.password` is a `String`; `FavoritesManager` wraps the favorite list in a fixed-key AES `SealedObject` with plaintext fallback. Preference proxy and certificate-store passwords are char arrays serialized without obfuscation. These are current persistence facts, not acceptable secrets-storage goals. Use only synthetic fixture state in tests ([JFTP.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/JFTP.java#L68), [JFTP.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/JFTP.java#L512), [FavoritesManager.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FavoritesManager.java#L112), [JFTPPreferences.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/JFTPPreferences.java#L40), [RemoteHost.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/RemoteHost.java#L39), [Favorite.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/Favorite.java#L25)).

## Key contracts

- `JFTPApplication.main` is the executable desktop entry point; `JFTPApplet` is a separate legacy applet launcher and an explicit compatibility question. Do not remove it or claim modern browser support without a target decision.
- `JFTP` owns global preferences, top-level menus/toolbars, tab management, window lifecycle and current-session routing. Keep selected-tab state and actions aligned.
- `FTPSession` owns connection/session state, FTP callbacks, directory panes, per-session filters and transfer-mode selection, recursive transfers, abort handling, status output, and temporary-file edit monitoring. It adapts to the external FTPAPI `FTPClient` / `ListParser` contract; the protocol is FTP or FTPS, not SFTP.
- `RemoteHost`/`Favorite` are serialized connection data. `FavoritesManager` and `JFTP.savePreferences/loadPreferences` own legacy local state formats. Preserve migration compatibility and never use real user-home credentials as test fixtures.
- Menus, toolbar and action classes are the user-visible command boundary. Preserve menu availability, keyboard accelerators, modal confirmations, active-session targeting, Desktop handoffs, drag/drop, and local versus remote filesystem effects.
- `JFTPPreferences`, connection dialogs and preference panels define transfer mapping/defaults, proxy, certificate store paths, security options, locale/theme and update settings. Do not conflate FTPS with SSH/SFTP or silently remove platform-specific behavior.

## Original baseline evidence and authority

The baseline has 576 tracked files: 182 Java sources and 394 non-Java paths. The three source-reading ledgers cover 79 support/security, 59 application/workflow, and 44 UI/browser Java files; the build/resources ledger records the remaining inventory and binary assets. The analysis and current-state pages are in [the documentation index](README.md). Analysis was static. The current environment report says Microsoft OpenJDK 21.0.10+7 is available and `mvn` is not recognized on this PowerShell `PATH`; no Maven wrapper exists in the repository. Maven dependency resolution, compilation, startup, test execution, GUI behavior, network behavior, and distribution launch remain unverified. The untracked `micro` file predates this work and stays untouched.

Use only synthetic preferences, favorites, certificates, keystores, local trees, and FTP server state in future verification. The real profile data directory is `${user.home}/.jftp/data`; preferences and favorites use Java serialization, preference passwords are serialized as char arrays, favorites wrap a password-bearing host list in fixed-key AES `SealedObject` with a plaintext fallback, and certificate stores default to JKS files under that directory. These are compatibility facts, not acceptable secret-storage goals. See [TLS and persistence](tls-and-persistence.md) before changing storage.

## Application preferences and favorites persistence

`JFTP.DATA_HOME` is `${user.home}/.jftp/data`; `preferences.ser` and `favorites.ser` are stored there. These locations are source facts reported from `JFTP.java` and `FavoritesManager.java` by the application-workflow analysis; this subtask did not read those application classes in full.

`JFTPPreferences` is stored as a Java-serialized object in `preferences.ser`. Certificate-store path fields are ordinary strings; server/client JKS passwords and proxy password are `char[]` fields. The default store paths are the two files above, and both store password arrays default to the literal `changeit`. No password obfuscation is applied to these preference fields before Java serialization. Other serialized fields include UI and connection configuration; exact serialization compatibility is tied to the class definition/serial UID and Java object graph. `preferences.ser` should be treated as sensitive local state, not a safe interchange format.

Favorites are also Java serialized. `RemoteHost.password` is a `String` in the serialized host object. `FavoritesManager` wraps the favorites object in `SealedObject` using `Cipher.getInstance("AES")` and a fixed hard-coded 16-byte key, then writes `favorites.ser`. If cipher setup is unavailable, code falls back to serializing the plaintext list. Reading an older plaintext-list format immediately rewrites it through the current save path. The fixed-key reversible wrapper is obfuscation, not meaningful protection from someone who can read the application and file. Do not copy real `preferences.ser`, favorites, passwords, or live keystores into fixtures or logs.

4. **FTPS certificate and trust decisions:** use loopback explicit/implicit FTPS and generated certificates; cover trusted connection, the untrusted host-matching prompt accept/reject path, expired/not-yet-valid, hostname mismatch, separately installed trust across restart, and handshake failure. Mark modern hostname/PKIX enforcement as a pending correction; unsafe acceptance is a defect, not a desired stable contract. Choose visible prompt/override policy explicitly.

UI-dependent cases must assert user-visible/session outcomes and relevant file or saved-state changes. Include Preferences panel validation and save/cancel/default behavior (noting that Software Updates “Check Now” begins immediately), connection field trim-to-validate but raw-value persistence, command/session selection routing, recursive remote-property working-directory restoration, and cancellation/close behavior where safe and deterministic. See [UI/browser details](ui-and-browser-details.md) for the source-grounded edge-case catalog; it refines these four suites and does not add a fifth.

These four are whole-application suites: unit assertions may support their deterministic data transformations, but suites 2–4 must cross the application/session/action or visible UI boundary when the behavior depends on FTP, browser, archive, or TLS orchestration. Assert destination bytes and paths, visible/session output, prompts, cancellation/status, or persisted compatibility—not helper classes, private fields, internal loops or thread counts. Use deterministic loopback servers, isolated homes and unique ports; no public servers, real secrets, remote customer files, or developer profile state.

3. **Preference/favorite compatibility fixture.** In a temporary user home, seed the serialized preference and favorite formats, including configured JKS paths, passwords, and a favorite with a password; load, save, restart, and confirm the existing values and files remain readable. Include legacy plaintext favorite-list migration and the AES-wrapped form. Do not use live user profile files or credentials.
4. **Text editing contract.** On the Swing EDT, insert mixed-case, over-limit, and multiline text into MTextField, MTextArea and MPasswordField; assert resulting text, beep-independent truncation, selection/focus behavior, clipboard action enablement where a controlled clipboard is available, and the password cut/copy/undo suppression. Use a private clipboard or skip clipboard-specific assertions only when the fixture cannot provide one; do not weaken core document output checks.

## Reproducible Windows commands

Run PowerShell from the repository root with JDK 21 on PATH. These commands use
an external Maven cache, empty settings and a synthetic application profile:

```powershell
$run = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'jftp-windows-startup'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $run -Force | Out-Null
$env:MAVEN_USER_HOME = Join-Path $run 'wrapper-cache'
Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $run 'settings.xml') -Value '<settings xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/SETTINGS/1.0.0"/>'
.\mvnw.cmd -B -ntp "-Dmaven.repo.local=$run\repository" -s "$run\settings.xml" test org.apache.maven.plugins:maven-dependency-plugin:3.8.1:copy-dependencies -DincludeScope=test
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'JFTP build/tests failed' }
$profile = Join-Path $run 'profile'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $profile -Force | Out-Null
java "-Duser.home=$profile" -cp 'target\test-classes;target\classes;target\dependency\*' com.myjavaworld.jftp.StartupStateProbe desktop-seed
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Synthetic profile setup failed' }
java "-Duser.home=$profile" -cp 'target\classes;target\dependency\*' com.myjavaworld.jftp.JFTPApplication
```

Test-scope dependency copying supports the synthetic-profile fixture; it does not
change application dependency scopes or distribution contents. The fixture creates
`files/hello.txt`, selects that directory, uses English UI and disables automatic
update checks only in the synthetic preferences. It rejects homes outside the OS
temporary directory before loading application state. Start a new JVM after seeding
because legacy classes snapshot `user.home` and preferences statically.

# Windows startup bootstrap

The user authorized a minimal Windows build/startup attempt and useful basic
regression tests on 2026-10-08. This slice retains the existing FTPAPI and JavaHelp,
Swing UI, applet source, resource roots and serialized data formats. Application
implementation bodies were not changed. It does not complete the four regression
suites or the broader modernization plan.

## Connection lifecycle and remote hosts

The connect action opens a connection dialog initialized from the current session host, or from global FTP client, listing parser, passive mode and TLS defaults. It has General, Security, Advanced and Commands tabs. Required host/user/password are checked using trimmed text, and port accepts 0 through 65535; approved values retain their original whitespace. Blank user/password populate as `anonymous` and the global email preference. The implicit-SSL port is validated only when implicit SSL is selected. Advanced settings preserve implementation class choices, initial local/remote directory text, passive mode and raw post-login commands ([UI and browser details](ui-and-browser-details.md#connection-and-preference-dialogs)). On approval, `FTPSession.connect` chooses the configured FTP client and listing parser by class name, applies passive mode, timeout, buffer size and TLS settings, attaches event listeners, opens the control connection, authenticates, sends host-specific commands, enters the configured initial remote directory, and lists it ([ConnectAction.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/actions/ConnectAction.java#L43), [FTPSession.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FTPSession.java#L617)). The session may prompt before replacing an existing connection; reconnect reuses the last `RemoteHost` ([FTPSession.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FTPSession.java#L593), [FTPSession.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FTPSession.java#L701)).

Do Not Encrypt Data Channel
Select this option to instructs JFTP not to use SSL for transferring actual data such as file transfers and directory listings. With this option selected, only commands that are sent over the command channel are encrypted, such as your user name and password.

At this point, you may click on the Add button to add the FTP site to your favorites or, click on the Advanced tab to configure advanced connect options.

Advanced Tab

The advanced connect options can be set by clicking on the Advanced tab in the Add Favorite FTP Site dialog.

FTP Client
Select the FTP client that you would like to use for connecting to this FTP site. This drop-down box contains the list of all installed FTP clients. You can see the list by clicking on the down arrow of the drop-down box. The default installation of JFTP comes with two different clients:

  • Default FTP Client
  • AS/400 FTP Client
The Default FTP Client works well with most FTP servers. The AS/400 FTP client is specifically designed for connecting to AS/400 FTP servers.

List Parser
Select a list parser that you would like to use for this FTP site. This drop-down box contains the list of all installed list parsers. A list parser is a small program used to parse the directory listing produced by an FTP server in response to the LIST command. The default installation of JFTP comes with the following two list parsers:

Favorites hold host label/address/port, user/password/account, FTP client and listing parser classes, initial local/remote directories, passive mode, login-time commands and SSL/data-channel choices. The manager sorts favorites, rejects duplicate names, supports add/edit/delete and connects the selected host in the active session (creating a session if none exists). `JFTP.DATA_HOME` is `${user.home}/.jftp/data`; global preferences and favorites are Java serialized files there. `JFTPPreferences` declares `serialVersionUID = 4316033315068041786L`, `RemoteHost` declares `-3213664402994404410L`, and `Favorite` declares `-8742993458243896488L`. The top-level saved containers are `JFTPPreferences` and the favorites list; `JFTP`/`FavoritesManager` define no additional explicit serialized-container version identifier. `RemoteHost.password` is a `String`; `FavoritesManager` wraps the favorite list in a fixed-key AES `SealedObject` with plaintext fallback. Preference proxy and certificate-store passwords are char arrays serialized without obfuscation. These are current persistence facts, not acceptable secrets-storage goals. Use only synthetic fixture state in tests ([JFTP.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/JFTP.java#L68), [JFTP.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/JFTP.java#L512), [FavoritesManager.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FavoritesManager.java#L112), [JFTPPreferences.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/JFTPPreferences.java#L40), [RemoteHost.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/RemoteHost.java#L39), [Favorite.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/Favorite.java#L25)).

Each `FTPSession` contains local and remote browser panes, a protocol transcript window, and a status bar. It keeps the current `FTPClient`, listing parser, local and remote working directories, filters, transfer-mode choice, abort flag, monitor state, and progress counters ([FTPSession.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FTPSession.java#L70)). The main frame routes menu commands to the currently selected tab, so active-tab selection and per-session transfer state are user-visible contracts ([JFTP.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/JFTP.java#L168)).

The connection boundary is the external `com.myjavaworld.ftp.FTPClient` API. `FTPSession.connect` reflectively constructs the selected client and `ListParser`, configures passive mode, timeout, buffer size, SSL mode and data-channel encryption, installs listeners, connects, logs in, issues configured commands, chooses the initial remote directory, and lists it ([FTPSession.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FTPSession.java#L617)). The source uses FTP and FTP over SSL/TLS (explicit, implicit, or SSL-if-available modes); it contains no SFTP client or SFTP protocol path. The FTP API artifact's current availability and redistribution rights remain unverified; preserve its adapter boundary until those questions are resolved.

The external client is FTPAPI's `FTPClient`. Source call sites cover `connect`, `login`, `disconnect`, `list`, `setWorkingDirectory`, `upload`, `download`, `createDirectory`, `createFile`, `rename`, `delete`, `executeCommand`, and `abort`. SSL/TLS modes are no SSL, SSL if available, explicit SSL and implicit SSL; the client also has a data-channel-unencrypted setting ([FavoritePropertiesDlg.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FavoritePropertiesDlg.java#L64), [FTPSession.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FTPSession.java#L634)). This is FTPS, not SFTP: no SSH/SFTP client or SFTP call path exists in the inspected application sources.

The connection transcript reports commands, replies and connection/error status. The status bar displays whether the FTP API reports the connection as secured, plus transfer/list progress, speed and elapsed time ([FTPSession.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FTPSession.java#L518), [StatusBar.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/StatusBar.java#L87)). SSL context construction calls `JFTPSSLContext.getSSLContext(jftp, host)` before the socket connection. Trust, certificate import and persistence behavior is detailed in [TLS and persistence](tls-and-persistence.md).

## Verification evidence

The initial failures were recorded independently: HTTP repository blocked by Maven;
unsupported Java 5 source/target; 12 compiler errors from Apple's legacy EAWT API;
JUnit 3.8.1 rejected by Surefire. Each received a bounded build/test configuration
change. These are bootstrap failures, not behavioral red tests.

The runner was checked with a temporary deliberately failing assertion: exactly
three tests were discovered, one failed with `Test discovery canary`, and none
were skipped. The assertion was then removed. The behavioral checks cover:

1. First-run preference creation, readable defaults and an empty favorites list.
2. Settings and synthetic password-bearing favorites surviving a separate JVM.
3. Base/German/Traditional Chinese bundles, icon, help-set location and configured
   FTP client/parser classes on the classpath.

These checks use a fresh temporary home per test and bounded child JVMs. They do
not prove browser operations, transfers, FTPS trust decisions or migration from
every historical saved-state variant.

Desktop QA uses the real `JFTPApplication.main`, synthetic state and AWT Robot
mouse/keyboard input. Logs and screenshots are retained outside the repository

Buffering is used to improve the performance when reading data from or writing data to files. Specify the buffer size to use while uploading or downloading files. The default installation sets this value to 64 Kilo Bytes.

Default Timeout
Specify the timeout in minutes. Timeout may be defined as the maximum time that JFTP waits for a server response. If no data is received in the specified amount of time, JFTP will disconnect from the FTP server. The default value of timeout is set to 5 minutes.

## Connection lifecycle and remote hosts

The connect action opens a connection dialog initialized from the current session host, or from global FTP client, listing parser, passive mode and TLS defaults. It has General, Security, Advanced and Commands tabs. Required host/user/password are checked using trimmed text, and port accepts 0 through 65535; approved values retain their original whitespace. Blank user/password populate as `anonymous` and the global email preference. The implicit-SSL port is validated only when implicit SSL is selected. Advanced settings preserve implementation class choices, initial local/remote directory text, passive mode and raw post-login commands ([UI and browser details](ui-and-browser-details.md#connection-and-preference-dialogs)). On approval, `FTPSession.connect` chooses the configured FTP client and listing parser by class name, applies passive mode, timeout, buffer size and TLS settings, attaches event listeners, opens the control connection, authenticates, sends host-specific commands, enters the configured initial remote directory, and lists it ([ConnectAction.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/actions/ConnectAction.java#L43), [FTPSession.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FTPSession.java#L617)). The session may prompt before replacing an existing connection; reconnect reuses the last `RemoteHost` ([FTPSession.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FTPSession.java#L593), [FTPSession.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FTPSession.java#L701)).

question.question: Which documented dependency provides the FTP API, and why is the original dependency setup not sufficient evidence of a working build?
question.notes: Dependency table identifies com.myjavaworld:ftpapi:3.0.0 and records unresolved availability/licensing; documentation is snapshot evidence.

results.text:
## Commit checkpoints and verification discipline

The coordinator owns commits and tracker updates. Delegates do not commit or push; the coordinator reviews and may commit their scoped outputs. Keep each logical step reviewable with explicit changed paths and descriptive commit messages: current-state documentation; test/fixture harness; each compile/bootstrap blocker; startup/resource correction; passing-test checkpoint; each Maven/plugin/dependency group; each Java API area; each TLS/archive/storage policy correction; and distribution assembly/launch fixes. Stage paths explicitly. Never bundle “cleanup everything” into one commit, and checkpoint before and after refactors. Use one execution record per change with command, environment, test count, outcome, output artifact/log path, and rollback hash.

The original baseline had no Maven wrapper or verified test command. The Windows bootstrap now provides both; see [the verified commands and limits](windows-startup.md). After a new execution instruction and after Maven/profile/toolchain setup, illustrative future commands could be `mvn -version`, `mvn -f pom.xml clean test`, and `mvn -f pom.xml clean package`; they are examples only, have not been executed, and are not established as working until prerequisites and profiles exist. Substitute the approved wrapper/tool path when selected. Distinguish unit, loopback integration, and visible GUI smoke evidence. A passing unit test cannot stand in for file transfer, FTPS prompting, packaged startup, or UI state.

## Original dependency and compatibility map

| Dependency or blocker | What it blocks | Required evidence or gate |
|---|---|---|
| Maven is not on the reported `PATH`; there is no wrapper or documented Maven profile | Reproducible compile, test, package, and distribution checks | In a later authorized phase, establish one approved Maven installation or project wrapper, record version and checksums/source, then run with isolated local repository/settings if needed. Do not download or install tools in this planning phase. |
| POM source/target `1.5`, `maven-compiler-plugin:2.4`, old Maven plugins/extensions and implicit lifecycle defaults | JDK 21 compilation and modern test execution may fail before application code is assessed | Capture the first reproducible failure. If required, make the smallest compiler/plugin/bootstrap change that allows current source and the tests to compile. Keep it separate from broad Java cleanup and document every intentional build-model change. |
| `com.myjavaworld:ftpapi:3.0.0` from the configured legacy HTTP repository; no jar is tracked and availability/license are unknown | Main application compilation and all real FTP/FTPS integration suites | Resolve provenance, artifact bytes, API surface, transitive dependencies, repository availability, and redistribution rights before replacement or distribution. Do not assume the original artifact is unavailable merely because it is not checked in. Do not replace it with a utility-only fake or direct FTPAPI tests. |

### Phase 2 — Minimum application startup, one blocker at a time

With the suite harness in place, repair only what is necessary for the desktop application to compile and start on the bootstrap JDK. Follow actual failures in dependency order: Maven/core model and source level; missing/legal dependency; direct Apple API compile blockers; classpath/resources/help; then startup. Keep the active reflective macOS path and menu behavior while evaluating `OSXAdapterOld`; preserve help IDs, locale bundles, applet entry point and resource paths until explicit compatibility choices are made.

Verify first startup, close/reopen settings from a fresh temporary home, visible main window and one session, help/resource lookup, and no destructive changes to profile state. Run the four suite smoke slices after each source/build change. Fix the help map mismatch only with a JavaHelp lookup check. Do not combine packaging, library replacement, secret-storage work or Swing redesign with startup repair.

**Validation artifacts:** exact compile/startup failure snapshots and corrections; dependency-resolution and license inventory; isolated first-run files; GUI/display and help smoke record; unchanged synthetic preference/favorite/JKS compatibility; updated tests.

**Gate:** JDK 21 compile/package and desktop startup succeed from a clean temporary home; no original feature was removed; the suites still pass except named fail-first corrections; every bootstrap change is attributable and documented.

**Rollback:** one commit per blocker/fix. Revert only the change that introduces a new failure; keep the test evidence and earlier known-good bootstrap checkpoint. Do not delete/migrate existing user data during rollback.

## Bootstrap, red/green and phase gates

Write these four suites before implementation changes. If the legacy code or test source cannot compile, make only the narrow compiler/tool/dependency bootstrap changes needed to make a baseline executable; then capture build and test output before launcher/startup fixes or broader changes. Resolve and document the FTPAPI artifact's availability, API surface and redistribution rights before replacing it. The old compiler plugin/source target, custom HTTP repository, unverified external FTP API, JavaHelp dependency, and package/launcher path mismatch can prevent a first compile or app launch; record each bootstrap failure separately from test failures. Do not claim the baseline is green until a build and each test layer actually runs.

For every implementation change, preserve the failing test output as red evidence, make the smallest behavior change, then capture the same test passing as green evidence. Keep characterization tests for existing behavior distinct from intended bug-fix tests. A known unsafe or incorrect behavior may be documented as a current defect and an expected fail-first security/correctness test; do not require preserving it. Do not change an assertion or remove a test only because a refactor regressed observable behavior.

## Outcome

The repository-map workflow works on this Windows checkout after isolated Python dependency setup. The current CI Rust mapper and frozen Python bundle both run here without a local build and produce byte-identical Java maps to the installed Python source. All 182 selected Java files parse with no reported parse failures; the 4096-unit budget selects 159 of 1,586 definitions. All 588 files under `src` retain their SHA-256 hashes after the checks.

The installed skill does **not** include either executable. CI already builds platform-specific programs, but delivery is source-only through this skill installation, with expiring Actions artifacts and a stale static CI link. At review time, the repository's Releases API returns an empty list. Downloading existing CI binaries is sufficient here; installing Rust or building locally is unnecessary for this use.

The full results include an initial missing-dependency failure, documentation defects, and six failed review expectations about a soft file limit. The latter were investigated and explicitly corrected below; they are not six mapper regressions. Real hard-failure invalidation subsequently passes for all three programs.

## Baseline

Inspection date: 2026-10-06. Working branch: `Luna-subagents-modernization`. Original revision: `14e62ce` (`Closes #8 - Row selection issues on Mac OS X`). The baseline has 576 tracked files, including 182 Java files and 394 other files. [The baseline manifest](analysis/repository-baseline.json) records original paths, modes and Git blob IDs. The pre-existing untracked `micro` file is outside the analysis and remains untouched.

This is a static-analysis and documentation phase. No application/build/resource file changes, test implementation, tool installation, application build, dependency resolution, application launch or test execution are authorized or performed here. Planned validation is not a passing result. Available local tooling was checked without building: Microsoft OpenJDK 21.0.10+7 LTS is on PATH; `mvn` is not recognized in the current PowerShell session.

No transitive dependency versions are asserted here: they are not pinned in this POM, and dependency resolution was not run. The declared repository is `jMethods` at `http://www.jMethods.com/mvn-repo`. Distribution management points to `ftp://ftp.kattare.com/jmethods_com/mvn-repo`, with `uniqueVersion=false`; SCM metadata names the historical GitHub project. Treat these as configured legacy endpoints, not verified live services (`pom.xml`, `repositories`, `distributionManagement`, and `scm`).

The exact build plugin declarations are `maven-compiler-plugin:2.4`, `maven-jar-plugin:2.4`, `maven-source-plugin:2.1.2`, `maven-assembly-plugin:2.3`, `maven-scm-plugin:1.7`, `maven-deploy-plugin:2.7`, and `maven-release-plugin:2.3`. The build extension is `org.apache.maven.wagon:wagon-ftp:2.2`. There is no Maven wrapper, parent POM, dependency management section, plugin management section, profile, toolchain declaration, or explicit Surefire configuration in the tracked POM. Maven defaults therefore remain implicit. The POM has a custom repository but no explicit plugin repository.

`maven-assembly-plugin` binds the `single` goal to `package`, using [src/main/assembly/binary.xml](../src/main/assembly/binary.xml). The descriptor produces `zip`, exploded `dir`, and `tar.gz`, includes a base directory, copies transitive dependency artifacts to `lib/`, copies project `target/*.jar` files to the distribution root excluding `*-sources.jar`, includes root `*.txt` and `*.md`, and copies/filters the configured script source directory (`binary.xml`). The jar manifest advertises `lib/` as its dependency classpath prefix and the application main class.

## Read in this order

| Document | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [Modernization plan](modernization-plan.md) | Ordered phases, prerequisites, validation gates, commit checkpoints and open decisions |
| [Fork and upstream workflow](git-workflow.md) | Clone setup, publishing to the personal fork and reviewing original-author changes |
| [Architecture](architecture.md) | Entry points, package boundaries, dependencies, threading and state |
| [Windows startup](windows-startup.md) | Reproducible isolated build/start, basic state tests and desktop evidence |
| [Build and dependencies](build-and-dependencies.md) | Exact declared Java/library/plugin versions, repositories and build constraints |
| [Application workflows](application-workflows.md) | Desktop/session/browser/transfer actions, preferences, favorites and auxiliary features |
| [UI and browser details](ui-and-browser-details.md) | Dialog validation, local/remote browser models, filtering, selection and preference controls |
| [Four behavioral regression suites](regression-test-design.md) | Detailed implementation-independent examples and fixture/validation strategy |
| [Shared support libraries](support-libraries.md) | Swing helpers, utilities, filesystem/event behavior and ZIP contracts |
| [TLS and persistence](tls-and-persistence.md) | Trust/key/certificate flows, storage compatibility and security limitations |
| [Security modernization options](security-modernization-options.md) | Brief FTP/FTPS/SFTP comparison, certificate inventory and researched version candidates |
| [Resources and distribution](resources-and-distribution.md) | Locales, assets, help, assembly, launch scripts and platform packaging |

## Build-related modernization boundaries

Follow the authoritative ordering and gates in [the integrated modernization plan](modernization-plan.md). These build-related boundaries are proposals, not evidence that the source compiles:

1. Design and implement the four behavioral suites before refactoring. Resolve the `ftpapi:3.0.0` legal/availability gate and establish reproducible Maven/JDK 21 tooling when implementation is authorized. Record actual resolution and failures; do not infer transitive dependencies. If compilation blocks test execution, isolate only the compiler/dependency/API bootstrap needed to make the characterization baseline executable.
2. Run the baseline suites, then repair minimum startup blockers while retaining FTP/FTPS, JavaHelp content, localized resources, manifest classpath and distribution forms. Run the same characterization cases after each change. Do not combine a source/API refactor or library replacement with this bootstrap.
3. When launcher layout prevents the intended startup route, reconcile assembly output, filtered substitutions, manifest classpath and both launchers as one isolated fix with tests before/after. Preserve zip, directory and tar.gz deliverables; final verification of every platform/archive remains a separate distribution phase.
4. After a passing test/startup checkpoint, introduce plugin and dependency upgrades individually with behavior comparisons, package checks and license review. Keep transfer/security, locale/help/resource and packaging coverage in place before replacing any old library.

## Verification limits

The coverage ledgers are delegate attestations checked against the tracked-file inventory; they are not execution traces or a proof every inferred behavior is correct. Binary images were not visually inspected. No Maven dependency tree, passing baseline tests, working FTP connection, usable GUI, compatible serialized-data round trip, or successful modern-JDK build is claimed. These require the later execution phase and its controlled fixtures.

question.question: What selection behavior must be preserved when replacing the file browser context menus?
question.notes: Right-clicking a selected row retains selection, while blank-area popup clears it.

results.text:
1. **Startup, session selection, preferences and favorites:** launch JFTP with isolated `user.home`; verify first-start defaults and one session; add/select multiple sessions; save/reload representative preference and favorite values; verify duplicate handling and synthetic password-bearing favorite persistence.
2. **Local and remote browser behavior:** on temporary local and controlled remote trees, cover pane navigation, roots/breadcrumbs, refresh, selection before/after sorting, selected-row versus blank-area context menus, filters (including hidden-file/exclusion inversion and lenient dates), create/rename/delete confirm and cancel, and visible listings. Add spaces, Unicode, and case-sensitive names where platform/server permits.
3. **Transfer and archive workflows:** invoke actual JFTP `FTPSession` transfer/archive actions, not FTPAPI-only helpers. First upload/download a binary fixture and assert exact bytes. Expand to ASCII conversion, renamed targets, recursion/filtering, manual/default mode, progress/status, permission/data-channel failures, and gated abort. Exercise archive temp/chosen destinations, deletion option, and traversal rejection. ZIP traversal rejection is an intended security correction and must remain tracked as expected-failing until fixed; do not claim all suites green by skipping or disabling it.

## Browser and file workflows

Each session presents local and remote file panes side by side above the protocol/status transcript. The local side starts from the saved local directory, falling back to the platform's default directory if it is missing. Connection may replace that starting directory with a host favorite's initial local directory. The remote side is populated after connect and changes with the FTP working directory. Local and remote filters are per-session and clearing a filter restores an unfiltered listing. Pane behavior includes multi-selection, header sorting, double-click/Enter navigation, keyboard delete, directory/link navigation, selection totals, and right-click context menus. A selected-row popup retains the current multi-selection; a blank-area popup clears it. Sorts act on the underlying data array without a separate row sorter, and descending order also places directories after files ([UI and browser details](ui-and-browser-details.md#browser-rows-selection-and-navigation)).

## Key contracts

- `JFTPApplication.main` is the executable desktop entry point; `JFTPApplet` is a separate legacy applet launcher and an explicit compatibility question. Do not remove it or claim modern browser support without a target decision.
- `JFTP` owns global preferences, top-level menus/toolbars, tab management, window lifecycle and current-session routing. Keep selected-tab state and actions aligned.
- `FTPSession` owns connection/session state, FTP callbacks, directory panes, per-session filters and transfer-mode selection, recursive transfers, abort handling, status output, and temporary-file edit monitoring. It adapts to the external FTPAPI `FTPClient` / `ListParser` contract; the protocol is FTP or FTPS, not SFTP.
- `RemoteHost`/`Favorite` are serialized connection data. `FavoritesManager` and `JFTP.savePreferences/loadPreferences` own legacy local state formats. Preserve migration compatibility and never use real user-home credentials as test fixtures.
- Menus, toolbar and action classes are the user-visible command boundary. Preserve menu availability, keyboard accelerators, modal confirmations, active-session targeting, Desktop handoffs, drag/drop, and local versus remote filesystem effects.
- `JFTPPreferences`, connection dialogs and preference panels define transfer mapping/defaults, proxy, certificate store paths, security options, locale/theme and update settings. Do not conflate FTPS with SSH/SFTP or silently remove platform-specific behavior.

### 2. Local and remote browser behavior

Use a dedicated temporary local tree and isolated remote fixture tree. Exercise changing/up-directory navigation, refresh, select-all/invert, independently applied and cleared filters, create file/directory, rename, confirmed delete, properties, and local/remote open behavior for files and directories. Check that cancelled dialogs leave the filesystem unchanged and that successful operations refresh the visible listing. After sorting, verify the selected file still corresponds to the intended row; exercise selected-row and blank-area context popups because one preserves multi-selection and the other clears it. Verify ascending/descending directory placement and the remote attributes column's unsortable behavior. Cover inclusion/exclusion, empty criteria, regex errors, lenient date input, the local hidden-file/exclusion interaction, and directory pass behavior. For remote tests, assert FTP server filesystem results and returned listing names; for local tests, assert only within the temporary fixture root.

4. **FTPS certificate and trust decisions:** use loopback explicit/implicit FTPS and generated certificates; cover trusted connection, the untrusted host-matching prompt accept/reject path, expired/not-yet-valid, hostname mismatch, separately installed trust across restart, and handshake failure. Mark modern hostname/PKIX enforcement as a pending correction; unsafe acceptance is a defect, not a desired stable contract. Choose visible prompt/override policy explicitly.

UI-dependent cases must assert user-visible/session outcomes and relevant file or saved-state changes. Include Preferences panel validation and save/cancel/default behavior (noting that Software Updates “Check Now” begins immediately), connection field trim-to-validate but raw-value persistence, command/session selection routing, recursive remote-property working-directory restoration, and cancellation/close behavior where safe and deterministic. See [UI/browser details](ui-and-browser-details.md) for the source-grounded edge-case catalog; it refines these four suites and does not add a fifth.

These four are whole-application suites: unit assertions may support their deterministic data transformations, but suites 2–4 must cross the application/session/action or visible UI boundary when the behavior depends on FTP, browser, archive, or TLS orchestration. Assert destination bytes and paths, visible/session output, prompts, cancellation/status, or persisted compatibility—not helper classes, private fields, internal loops or thread counts. Use deterministic loopback servers, isolated homes and unique ports; no public servers, real secrets, remote customer files, or developer profile state.

# Java source instructions

This subtree contains the existing Java application and shared packages under `com.myjavaworld`. Read the [root instructions](../../../AGENTS.md), [architecture](../../../docs/architecture.md), and the nearest package-level `AGENTS.md` before editing.

Application/session behavior belongs to `jftp`; command wiring belongs to `jftp/actions`; TLS belongs to `jftp/ssl`; reusable widgets belong to `gui`; shared file/resource/event helpers belong to `util`; archives belong to `zip`. Preserve desktop behavior and source/resource relationships. Keep UI work on the appropriate Swing thread and characterize asynchronous error/cancellation behavior before replacing workers. Do not combine library substitution, storage migration and unrelated language cleanup in one change. Follow [the test-scope guidance](../../test/AGENTS.md) for characterization tests and [Windows startup](../../../docs/windows-startup.md) for the existing bootstrap. A documentation-only task does not authorize test implementation.

# JFTP action instructions

Actions under this package connect menus and toolbar gestures to `JFTP`, the selected `FTPSession`, dialogs and file/remote operations. Read [application workflows](../../../../../../../docs/application-workflows.md) and [regression test design](../../../../../../../docs/regression-test-design.md) before changing a user-visible action.

Preserve each action's active-session selection, connection/selection preconditions, cancellation behavior, confirmation prompts, destination-name handling, worker completion refresh and status/error reporting. Remote open/edit/print downloads a temporary file; monitored edits can upload a changed file to the original remote path. Archive actions bridge `FTPSession` with the sibling `zip` package. `AbortAction` sets the session abort flag and calls `FTPClient.abort()`; recursive transfer loops check between items. The API is FTP/FTPS; do not substitute SFTP semantics.

Prefer tests at the application action/session boundary. Use temporary user homes and local roots plus deterministic controlled FTP/FTPS fixtures. Assert resulting local/server files, user-visible state, cancellation/error outcomes and callbacks, not action internals or thread classes. Separate existing behavior characterization from explicit bug-fix expectations for security defects.

Whenever source structure, implementation responsibilities, commands, dependencies or public behavior change, update the applicable root/package/action `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` instructions and affected `docs/` files in the same change. `CLAUDE.md` imports this file.

## Behavior risks and regression examples

The following are observed contracts or edges to preserve during a behavior-preserving rewrite. Intentional changes should be identified as such, because otherwise they can hide features or change established handling:

- Local/remote panes keep multi-selection through row popups but clear it on blank-area popups; selection index semantics currently assume no row sorter. Exercise selection after sort, keyboard open/delete, double-click on file vs directory/link, and right-click on selected vs blank space.
- Descending sort moves directories below files; equal local dates may compare equal. Case folding depends on the JVM default locale. Exercise same-name case variants, locale changes, same-size/timestamp ties, and filesystem roots.
- Filters use regexes against basenames, optional `yyyy-MM-dd` date bounds, lenient date parsing, and inclusion/exclusion inversion. Exercise empty criteria, invalid regex, overflow/normalized dates, hidden-file exclusion interaction, and the directory-always-pass rule.
- Connection validates by trimming to check required fields but keeps entered strings intact; paths and commands are passed through verbatim. Test whitespace, Unicode, bracketed IPv6/host strings, port endpoints 0/65535, missing/invalid ports, and implicit SSL's conditional port validation.
- Local properties recurse through filtered contents and remote properties temporarily mutate/restore working directory. Test cancellation/close mid-traversal, list errors, null local listing, symlinks/links, `.`/`..`, permission preservation, and exact remote cwd restoration.

## Test layers and evidence

Use pure unit tests for deterministic value transformations and isolated state rules: extension-to-transfer-type selection, remote-host settings, favorite duplicate identity, filter decisions, resource-bundle lookup and help-map references. Unit tests should not stand in for the transfer contract.

Use integration tests that invoke JFTP application/session actions against a controlled loopback FTP server for session, file, transfer and FTPS contracts. Keep all input/output under a per-test temporary user home and temporary local tree. Configure a deterministic server fixture with fixed response sequences, passive data ports, an isolated remote filesystem, and explicit binary and ASCII behavior. Avoid public servers, user home state, network dependencies and shared ports. The fixture must expose server-side files and control/data command outcomes so assertions cover observable output and state.

Use UI smoke tests for startup, tab/session navigation, preferences/favorites dialogs, help, status display, Desktop handoff where the OS supports it, certificate prompts, and menu/toolbar enablement. Run headless only for tests that do not require native desktop services. Do not claim Java applet/browser smoke support on a current JDK; treat the applet target as a compatibility question.

This package contains reusable Swing components, document models, renderers, themes, and the legacy worker used by application and certificate screens. question.question: What polls locally edited files and notifies listeners when their modification timestamp increases?
question.notes: A one-second Swing Timer checks lastModified and dispatches FileChangeEvent to registered listeners.

results.text:
[`FileUtilities.copyFile`](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/util/FileUtilities.java#L30) copies bytes through 4 KiB buffered streams and opens the target with `FileOutputStream`, overwriting it. It does not create parent directories, preserve metadata, or stage atomically. `SystemUtil` snapshots OS/JRE/user-home/working-directory properties once during class initialization; unavailable properties become `Unknown`, and its macOS check looks for `Mac OS X` in `os.name`.

`FileChangeMonitor` stores `File` keys and initial `lastModified()` values in a `Hashtable`. Adding the first file starts a one-second Swing `Timer`; timer callbacks therefore run on the Swing event dispatch thread. It reports only when the observed timestamp strictly increases. It does not report deletion, creation with unchanged/older time, content changes with preserved timestamp, or timestamp decrease. `remove` does not stop the timer when the set becomes empty; `stopMonitor` stops the timer but leaves registrations in place; because it retains the non-null stopped timer, later `add` calls do not restart monitoring. Listener callbacks run synchronously in reverse listener-registration order on the timer's EDT. A slow listener blocks the UI. `FileChangeEvent` exposes mutable public fields and getters, including the existing lowercase-n getter `getnewDate()`.

`ProgressEvent` and `StatusEvent` are simple immutable-by-interface `EventObject` payloads, with `ProgressListener` and `StatusListener` callback interfaces. The ZIP code uses the same progress event type.

## Connection lifecycle and remote hosts

The connect action opens a connection dialog initialized from the current session host, or from global FTP client, listing parser, passive mode and TLS defaults. It has General, Security, Advanced and Commands tabs. Required host/user/password are checked using trimmed text, and port accepts 0 through 65535; approved values retain their original whitespace. Blank user/password populate as `anonymous` and the global email preference. The implicit-SSL port is validated only when implicit SSL is selected. Advanced settings preserve implementation class choices, initial local/remote directory text, passive mode and raw post-login commands ([UI and browser details](ui-and-browser-details.md#connection-and-preference-dialogs)). On approval, `FTPSession.connect` chooses the configured FTP client and listing parser by class name, applies passive mode, timeout, buffer size and TLS settings, attaches event listeners, opens the control connection, authenticates, sends host-specific commands, enters the configured initial remote directory, and lists it ([ConnectAction.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/actions/ConnectAction.java#L43), [FTPSession.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FTPSession.java#L617)). The session may prompt before replacing an existing connection; reconnect reuses the last `RemoteHost` ([FTPSession.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FTPSession.java#L593), [FTPSession.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FTPSession.java#L701)).

## Connection and preference dialogs

[ConnectionDlg](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/ConnectionDlg.java) has General, Security, Advanced, and Commands tabs. General requires trimmed non-empty host/user/password and validates the port as an integer in the inclusive 0–65535 range. `setRemoteHost(null)` supplies a fresh host object; when populating, blank user becomes `anonymous` and blank password becomes the global email preference. The saved host/user/password strings are not trimmed after validation. Security choices are no SSL, SSL if available, explicit SSL, and implicit SSL; the implicit SSL port is range-checked only in that mode. The “Do Not Encrypt Data Channel” checkbox maps directly to the data-channel-unencrypted property. The Security panel initially selects no SSL before `setRemoteHost` populates any provided host settings. Advanced preserves FTP client and parser implementation choices, initial local/remote directory text, passive mode, and raw post-login command text.

The external client is FTPAPI's `FTPClient`. Source call sites cover `connect`, `login`, `disconnect`, `list`, `setWorkingDirectory`, `upload`, `download`, `createDirectory`, `createFile`, `rename`, `delete`, `executeCommand`, and `abort`. SSL/TLS modes are no SSL, SSL if available, explicit SSL and implicit SSL; the client also has a data-channel-unencrypted setting ([FavoritePropertiesDlg.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FavoritePropertiesDlg.java#L64), [FTPSession.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FTPSession.java#L634)). This is FTPS, not SFTP: no SSH/SFTP client or SFTP call path exists in the inspected application sources.

The connection transcript reports commands, replies and connection/error status. The status bar displays whether the FTP API reports the connection as secured, plus transfer/list progress, speed and elapsed time ([FTPSession.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FTPSession.java#L518), [StatusBar.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/StatusBar.java#L87)). SSL context construction calls `JFTPSSLContext.getSSLContext(jftp, host)` before the socket connection. Trust, certificate import and persistence behavior is detailed in [TLS and persistence](tls-and-persistence.md).

Each `FTPSession` contains local and remote browser panes, a protocol transcript window, and a status bar. It keeps the current `FTPClient`, listing parser, local and remote working directories, filters, transfer-mode choice, abort flag, monitor state, and progress counters ([FTPSession.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FTPSession.java#L70)). The main frame routes menu commands to the currently selected tab, so active-tab selection and per-session transfer state are user-visible contracts ([JFTP.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/JFTP.java#L168)).

The connection boundary is the external `com.myjavaworld.ftp.FTPClient` API. `FTPSession.connect` reflectively constructs the selected client and `ListParser`, configures passive mode, timeout, buffer size, SSL mode and data-channel encryption, installs listeners, connects, logs in, issues configured commands, chooses the initial remote directory, and lists it ([FTPSession.java](../src/main/java/com/myjavaworld/jftp/FTPSession.java#L617)). The source uses FTP and FTP over SSL/TLS (explicit, implicit, or SSL-if-available modes); it contains no SFTP client or SFTP protocol path. The FTP API artifact's current availability and redistribution rights remain unverified; preserve its adapter boundary until those questions are resolved.

## Key contracts

- `JFTPApplication.main` is the executable desktop entry point; `JFTPApplet` is a separate legacy applet launcher and an explicit compatibility question. Do not remove it or claim modern browser support without a target decision.
- `JFTP` owns global preferences, top-level menus/toolbars, tab management, window lifecycle and current-session routing. Keep selected-tab state and actions aligned.
- `FTPSession` owns connection/session state, FTP callbacks, directory panes, per-session filters and transfer-mode selection, recursive transfers, abort handling, status output, and temporary-file edit monitoring. It adapts to the external FTPAPI `FTPClient` / `ListParser` contract; the protocol is FTP or FTPS, not SFTP.
- `RemoteHost`/`Favorite` are serialized connection data. `FavoritesManager` and `JFTP.savePreferences/loadPreferences` own legacy local state formats. Preserve migration compatibility and never use real user-home credentials as test fixtures.
- Menus, toolbar and action classes are the user-visible command boundary. Preserve menu availability, keyboard accelerators, modal confirmations, active-session targeting, Desktop handoffs, drag/drop, and local versus remote filesystem effects.
- `JFTPPreferences`, connection dialogs and preference panels define transfer mapping/defaults, proxy, certificate store paths, security options, locale/theme and update settings. Do not conflate FTPS with SSH/SFTP or silently remove platform-specific behavior.

- **FTP library option:** verify FTPAPI 3.0.0 provenance, API, license and redistribution rights first. If replacement is needed, Apache Commons Net **3.13.0** is an official Java 8+ FTP/FTPS candidate. Its FTPS hostname verification is off by default, so enable and test it. Compare parsers, callbacks, ASCII, passive/active modes and data-channel protection. ([release](https://commons.apache.org/proper/commons-net/changes.html), [Java requirement](https://commons.apache.org/proper/commons-net/download_net.html), [FTPS API](https://commons.apache.org/proper/commons-net/apidocs/org/apache/commons/net/ftp/FTPSClient.html))

New product functionality, outside modernization; do not bundle with FTPAPI replacement. ([releases](https://mina.apache.org/downloads-sshd.html), [project](https://mina.apache.org/sshd-project/), [2.20.0 notes](https://mina.apache.org/sshd-project/download_2.20.0.html))

# FTP, FTPS, SFTP, and certificate direction

Research checked 2026-10-06. Candidates only; no new feature is authorized.

- **Current protocols:** built-in modes cover plain FTP (no TLS) and FTPS (SSL-if-available, explicit, implicit); FTPS data may be unencrypted. No in-tree SSH/SFTP is evidenced, though a reflective custom FTP client could add protocols. FTPS uses TLS and the app's X.509/JKS trust path ([RFC 4217](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4217)); SFTP runs over SSH and uses SSH host-key trust ([RFC 4251](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4251)).
- **Asset inventory:** tracked metadata has zero certificate/key/store suffix matches (`.pem`, `.crt`, `.cer`, `.der`, `.p12`, `.pfx`, `.jks`, `.keystore`, `.pub`, `.key`, `.p7b`, `.p7c`). An existence-only check on 2026-10-06 found default profile files `~/.jftp/data/serverCertificates.jks` and `clientCertificates.jks` absent. No contents were read; system stores, custom paths and other locations were not inventoried. The UI imports X.509 certificate entries, not private keys.
- **FTPS direction:** prefer TLS 1.3, retain TLS 1.2 for interoperability, and prohibit TLS 1.0/1.1 ([RFC 9846](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9846/), [RFC 8996](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8996/)). The `SSL` algorithm alias is not proof of SSLv3 configuration; negotiated TLS is unknown without a handshake. Correct chain/hostname validation and decide visible trust-prompt changes; do not globally weaken TLS for legacy servers.

Protocol/source and repository-asset evidence, plus primary-source options for TLS, FTP client maintenance, and optional SFTP, are summarized in [security modernization options](security-modernization-options.md). In this checkout, built-in support evidenced by source is FTP/FTPS; no runtime TLS version is proven, and SFTP would be a separate new feature outside this plan.

# TLS, certificate UI, and keystore boundary

This package owns the application's SSL context, X.509 key/trust managers, certificate dialogs, and JKS persistence adapter. It is part of the existing JFTP application, not an independent module. Read the [repository instructions](../../../../../../../AGENTS.md), [Java boundary instructions](../../../../AGENTS.md), the application/session instructions ([jftp](../AGENTS.md)), [TLS and persistence notes](../../../../../../../docs/tls-and-persistence.md), and [brief protocol/certificate modernization options](../../../../../../../docs/security-modernization-options.md) before changing this package. FTPS uses TLS/X.509; SFTP uses SSH and has no built-in implementation here. Adding SFTP requires separate feature scope and SSH host-key verification rather than reusing JKS trust decisions.

Preserve existing FTPS modes, certificate view/install/manage flows, configured keystore paths/passwords, JKS compatibility, and caller-visible failures until isolated fixtures characterize them. The current custom trust path validates only the first certificate's validity, compares only the leaf CN with the host, accepts on user Yes despite failed checks, and does not invoke delegate PKIX validation. Treat these as security defects; a secure correction must validate chains and hostnames correctly. Make the visible override/prompt policy an explicit product decision, retain the separate Install action semantics, and add controlled local FTPS regression coverage before changing it.

# JFTP action instructions

Actions under this package connect menus and toolbar gestures to `JFTP`, the selected `FTPSession`, dialogs and file/remote operations. Read [application workflows](../../../../../../../docs/application-workflows.md) and [regression test design](../../../../../../../docs/regression-test-design.md) before changing a user-visible action.

Preserve each action's active-session selection, connection/selection preconditions, cancellation behavior, confirmation prompts, destination-name handling, worker completion refresh and status/error reporting. Remote open/edit/print downloads a temporary file; monitored edits can upload a changed file to the original remote path. Archive actions bridge `FTPSession` with the sibling `zip` package. `AbortAction` sets the session abort flag and calls `FTPClient.abort()`; recursive transfer loops check between items. The API is FTP/FTPS; do not substitute SFTP semantics.

Prefer tests at the application action/session boundary. Use temporary user homes and local roots plus deterministic controlled FTP/FTPS fixtures. Assert resulting local/server files, user-visible state, cancellation/error outcomes and callbacks, not action internals or thread classes. Separate existing behavior characterization from explicit bug-fix expectations for security defects.

Whenever source structure, implementation responsibilities, commands, dependencies or public behavior change, update the applicable root/package/action `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` instructions and affected `docs/` files in the same change. `CLAUDE.md` imports this file.

JFTP is a legacy Java Swing FTP/FTPS application being modernized as a Codex + GitHub Copilot course exercise. Preserve existing functionality and saved user data. Adding SFTP, removing legacy entry points, or changing visible trust policies requires an explicit scope decision.
